    • withStandardComponent

      public OilAssayCharacterisation.AssayCut withStandardComponent(String componentName)
      Mark this mass-basis assay cut as an authoritative NeqSim standard component.

      Standard components use the attached thermodynamic system's component database and molar mass. They are added with SystemInterface.addComponent(String, double) rather than the petroleum pseudo-component correlation. Density, boiling-point, Watson-factor, and explicit molar-mass inputs are therefore not applicable and fail during preflight.

      Parameters:
      componentName - exact NeqSim standard-component identifier
      Returns:
      this cut

    • withDensity

      public OilAssayCharacterisation.AssayCut withDensity(double density)
      Set petroleum density using the legacy flexible input convention.

      Values up to 1.5 are interpreted as specific gravity (numerically g/cm3). Values above 1.5 are interpreted as kg/m3 and divided by 1000. New code should prefer withSpecificGravity(double) or withDensityKgPerCubicMetre(double).

      Parameters:
      density - specific gravity/g/cm3 or density in kg/m3
      Returns:
      this cut

    • withApiGravity

      public OilAssayCharacterisation.AssayCut withApiGravity(double apiGravity)
      Set API gravity at the conventional 60 degF reference.

      Negative API gravities are valid for liquids denser than water; only values at or below -131.5 are rejected because the API conversion becomes undefined.

      Parameters:

      Returns:

    • withWatsonCharacterizationFactor

      public OilAssayCharacterisation.AssayCut withWatsonCharacterizationFactor(double watsonFactor)
      Set an explicit UOP/Watson characterization factor for deriving the representative boiling point.

      When no representative boiling point is supplied, the cut resolves it from T_b = (K_W SG)^3 / 1.8, where T_b is in K and SG is the existing dimensionless specific-gravity view. An explicit representative boiling point and Watson factor are mutually exclusive so the authoritative source is unambiguous.

      Parameters:
      watsonFactor - dimensionless UOP/Watson characterization factor
      Returns:
      this cut

    • getWatsonCharacterizationFactor

      public double getWatsonCharacterizationFactor()
      Calculate or return the UOP/Watson characterization factor for this assay cut.

      The calculation uses K_W = (1.8 T_b)^(1/3) / SG, where T_b is the representative normal boiling point in K and SG is dimensionless specific gravity. This is equivalent to using the boiling point in degrees Rankine. A configured boiling interval uses its arithmetic midpoint through resolveAverageBoilingPoint().

      Returns:
      dimensionless UOP/Watson characterization factor
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if density or representative boiling point is unavailable, or the result is invalid

    • resolveMolarMass

      public double resolveMolarMass(double density, double boilingPointKelvin)
      Resolve the cut molar mass.

      If no explicit molar mass is stored, the existing NeqSim inverse petroleum correlation is used with density and representative boiling point. The inverse petroleum correlation returns a g/mol-sized value, which is converted to the kg/mol unit required by SystemInterface.addTBPfraction(String, double, double, double).

      Parameters:
      density - specific gravity / g/cm3 numeric value
      boilingPointKelvin - representative boiling point in K
      Returns:
      molar mass in kg/mol
